reasons: The page falls back to project p-003 when no id is given, which can show the wrong project.
The missing-data screen names test project ids, which would confuse a real user.
The Refresh project button is not restricted to admins in the code shown.
No tests are visible for this file.
Many values are untyped, so data mistakes may appear only at runtime.

terms.meaning: A reusable piece of the screen, such as a tab or a card, that is drawn wherever it is used.
A built-in React helper that lets a component remember values or fetch data while it is on screen.
Values the page remembers while it runs, such as which tab is open or whether a panel is shown.
Saved sample data used for testing or demos instead of live data.
A text format that turns plain lines into a diagram, used here for the relationship chart.
A value whose kind is not declared, so the compiler cannot check it.

used_by: Not visible in the code shown

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and page setup
sections.what: Brings in the shared pieces this page uses, including the evidence panels, data helpers, display helpers, colors and icons.
sections.why: Likely reason: collects everything the page needs in one place at the top of the file.
sections.watch_out: Imports use both relative paths and an alias, so moving a shared file can break one of the two styles.

sections.name: TabKey
sections.title: Names of the page tabs
sections.what: Lists the fifteen tab names the project page can show, from overview to values.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops a mistyped tab name from being used anywhere on the page.
sections.watch_out: A new tab must be added here, in the labels list, and in the drawing list, or it will not appear correctly.

sections.name: TAB_LABELS
sections.title: Tab titles shown to readers
sections.what: Gives each tab name its visible label, such as Delivery and Parties or Lessons Learnt.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The tab bar draws tabs in this list's order, so reordering here changes the screen.

sections.name: TrendIcon
sections.title: Trend arrow icon
sections.what: Shows a green up arrow for an upward trend, a red down arrow for a downward trend, and a grey flat line for anything else.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Any value other than UP or DOWN, including a typo, shows as flat.

sections.name: ScoreBar
sections.title: Score progress bar
sections.what: Draws a thin bar showing a score out of five. The bar turns red when the score is under 40 percent of the maximum.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The bar width is not capped, so a score above the maximum would spill past the bar.

sections.name: MilestoneStatusIcon
sections.title: Milestone status icon
sections.what: Shows a check mark for completed milestones, a clock for pending ones, a crossed circle for not applicable, and an empty circle for anything else.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A new status name will fall through to the empty circle, which may hide that it is new.

sections.name: AuditField
sections.title: Hover note on verified values
sections.what: Wraps a value in a dotted underline with a tooltip. The tooltip says Verified data point unless another label is given.
sections.why: Likely reason: signals to readers that the value has been checked.
sections.watch_out: Any value wrapped without a label is shown as verified, even if no one has checked it.

sections.name: DelayValue
sections.title: Delay value with approximate flag
sections.what: Shows a delay in months with a tilde and a small approx tag when the value is approximate. It can also show a note below the value.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The note appears only when the value is approximate and the show-note setting is on, so a note can be hidden silently.

sections.name: CitedField
sections.title: Field value with evidence popover
sections.what: Shows one project field with its first evidence item. Empty values show N/A, and the full citation opens from the evidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives each field a visible link to where its value came from.
sections.watch_out: Only the first evidence item for a field is used, so any others are not reachable from this field.

sections.name: formatDate
sections.title: Date display formatting
sections.what: Turns a stored date into a readable US-style date such as Mar 5, 2026, and shows N/A when the date is missing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Date-only text is read as UTC, so in some time zones the shown day can be one day earlier.

sections.name: computeDelta
sections.title: Days between planned and actual
sections.what: Counts the days from the planned date to the actual date and shows them as a signed number such as plus 12 days, or N/A if either date is missing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: It uses the same date reading as the date formatter, so the same time-zone shift can affect the count.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 1)
sections.title: Loading the project and its state
sections.what: Loads the project by its id from the web address, converts it for display, and checks research status every five seconds while a run is active. It also sets up the refresh action and remembers the open tab and open panels.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the data and the page's memory together before anything is drawn.
sections.watch_out: If no id is in the address, the page quietly loads project p-003 instead of showing an error.

sections.name: ProjectDetail: if
sections.title: Loading and missing-data screens
sections.what: Shows a spinner while the project loads. If no project is found, it shows a message saying detailed fixture data is not available and lists test ids. It also sets up opening the evidence side panel.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The message names test project ids, and any failed fetch looks the same as a project that does not exist.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 3)
sections.title: Budget and page header
sections.what: Works out the budget text, preferring a stated range, then free text, then a planned figure. It then draws the header with status badges, project name, description and the source review.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: When no budget exists, the page shows three dashes instead of N/A, which is inconsistent with other fields.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 4)
sections.title: Refresh button and key figures
sections.what: Shows a Refresh project button that starts research and changes its label while the run is active. It also shows when the project was last refreshed and a row of key figures such as budget, capacity, likelihood and confidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a user update the project's data and see at a glance how far along it is.
sections.watch_out: The button is not limited to admins in the code shown, and likelihood below 50 or confidence below 60 turns red.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 5)
sections.title: Tab bar and tab routing
sections.what: Draws the row of tab buttons and shows the content of the selected tab, passing each tab the data it needs.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Some tabs receive the raw project data and others receive the converted version, so passing the wrong one drops fields.

sections.name: ProjectDetail (part 6)
sections.title: Citation side panels
sections.what: Renders two citation side panels, one for evidence and one for update links, and closes the page.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Closing the update panel also clears its selected citation, but closing the evidence panel does not.

sections.name: SectionHeading
sections.title: Section heading style
sections.what: Draws a small uppercase heading with a cyan dot or a custom icon before the text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: CANONICAL_ROLE_ORDER
sections.title: Preferred order of company roles
sections.what: Lists the company roles in the order they should appear on the ecosystem view, starting with owner, then operator, then EPC.
sections.why: Likely reason: puts the most important roles at the top of the ecosystem view.
sections.watch_out: Roles missing from this list still appear, but at the end in alphabetical order.

sections.name: EcosystemTab (part 1)
sections.title: Ecosystem data and diagram text
sections.what: Loads the companies linked to the project, shows loading and empty states, sorts the roles, and builds the text for a relationship diagram with the project at the center and each company joined by its role.
sections.why: Likely reason: the diagram is written as text so it can be drawn from the company list automatically.
sections.watch_out: The diagram text removes some characters, including angle brackets, braces and quotes, so company names can show with characters missing.

sections.name: EcosystemTab (part 2)
sections.title: Ecosystem tab company groups and diagram
sections.what: Shows the companies linked to a project, grouped by their role, with a confidence percentage and a source link for each. Below the groups it draws a relationship diagram from the graph text.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reader see who plays which role in the project at a glance, and see how they connect.
sections.watch_out: The groups depend on sortedRoles, byRole and graph being built earlier in the same function (lines 499 to 546, not shown here), so changes there break this part.

sections.name: OverviewTab (part 1)
sections.title: Overview key facts grid
sections.what: Shows the headline facts for the project: country, technology, units, capacity, key dates, and delay. When a revised COD exists, the old date is struck through and the new date is shown in red.
sections.why: Likely reason: the most important facts are shown first so a reader gets the summary before the detail.
sections.watch_out: Missing values show the text '[ N/A ]', and the delay only appears when delayMonths is set, so a zero or missing value changes what the reader sees.

sections.name: OverviewTab (part 2)
sections.title: Overview intelligence fields and budget
sections.what: Shows who the vendor, EPC contractor and operator are, plus delivery model, ecosystem and strategy. Each value can be clicked to open its evidence. A budget panel shows low and high estimates in billions of dollars when those figures exist, along with currency notes and value caveats.
sections.why: Likely reason: each field is tied to its source so the reader can check where the claim came from.
sections.watch_out: The budget figures are divided by 1000 before display, which suggests the stored numbers are in millions of dollars. If the stored unit changes, every budget shown becomes wrong by a factor of 1000.

sections.name: OverviewTab (part 3)
sections.title: Overview cost and schedule variances
sections.what: When variance data exists, shows two cards. The cost card lists planned cost, actual cost and the percentage change, with red highlights for large overruns. The schedule card lists planned and actual duration, the delay, and any reason given.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes overruns visible, since those are the main concern for a project reader.
sections.watch_out: Two different thresholds are used: the cost card colours its accent red above 20 percent but colours the actual value red above 10 percent, so the two signals can disagree.

sections.name: OverviewTab (part 4)
sections.title: Confidence score bar
sections.what: Shows the overall confidence score as a large number with a bar underneath. The bar turns red below 50, amber below 75, and the main colour otherwise.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick sense of how much the data can be trusted.
sections.watch_out: The bar width is set directly from the score as a percentage, so a score above 100 or below 0 would overflow or disappear.

sections.name: OverviewTab (part 5)
sections.title: Success story facts and quotes
sections.what: When a success story exists, shows its key facts and takeaways as numbered lists, then a set of quotes. Each quote is a button that opens its evidence, showing the exact words, publisher and date.
sections.why: Likely reason: the quotes are tied to evidence so each claim can be checked against the original source.
sections.watch_out: The date is shown with new Date(q.date), so a missing or badly formatted date will display as an invalid date.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 1)
sections.title: Updates tab state setup
sections.what: Sets up the memory the Updates tab needs: which update is being edited, the new update form fields, and the status of an automatic research run. It also reads the list of updates for the project.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tab has several independent forms and progress messages, so each one keeps its own state.
sections.watch_out: There are many separate state values. A forgotten reset in one of them leaves old text or a stuck spinner on screen.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 2)
sections.title: Automatic update research and polling
sections.what: When an admin starts research, the tab asks the server for a research job, then checks its progress every two seconds. It shows the current step, and when the job finishes it reports how many updates were added. Common failures such as cooldown or a job already running get friendly messages.
sections.why: Likely reason: research runs on the server and can take a while, so the screen keeps asking for progress rather than waiting.
sections.watch_out: The polling repeats until the job completes or fails, and no time limit is visible, so a job that never finishes keeps the spinner running forever.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 3)
sections.title: Saving links and creating updates
sections.what: Saves a changed link for an existing update, where an empty value removes the link. Also sends a new update to the server with its date, headline, source, optional link, excerpt and locator, then clears the form and refreshes the list.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets admins fix or add links and records without leaving the page.
sections.watch_out: Save failures are only written to the browser console, so the user sees nothing when a save fails.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 4)
sections.title: Updates tab header and admin buttons
sections.what: Shows the News Feed heading. Admins see the Refresh Updates and Add Update buttons, and the research status and result banners appear beneath the header.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the controls for changing updates visible only to admins.
sections.watch_out: The buttons are hidden with the isAdmin flag only, so the server must also check permissions or a non-admin could still send changes.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 5)
sections.title: Error banner and new update form fields
sections.what: Shows any research error with a dismiss button. Then shows the add form with date, source, headline, optional link and optional excerpt fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form collects the minimum facts needed for a credible update record.
sections.watch_out: The Save button stays disabled until date, source and headline are filled, but the link and excerpt are optional, so they can be left blank.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 6)
sections.title: Locator picker and form buttons
sections.what: Lets the user pick where the evidence sits in the source (none, a text fragment, a PDF page or an anchor) and type the matching value. The Save and Cancel buttons follow.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reader jump straight to the exact passage in the source.
sections.watch_out: A locator is saved only when both a type and a value are filled. Picking a type and leaving the value empty silently saves no locator.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 7)
sections.title: Updates timeline list
sections.what: Shows a timeline of updates, each with its date, source and a Linked badge when a link exists. Admins get an Edit or Add link button, and the inline link editor opens beneath the headline.
sections.why: Likely reason: a timeline reads naturally for news that happened over time.
sections.watch_out: The edit button sits inside a clickable card. The code stops the click from spreading so the card does not open by accident, and removing that stop would cause this.

sections.name: UpdatesTab (part 8)
sections.title: Inline link editor controls
sections.what: Closes the inline link editor. Pressing Enter in the link box saves it, and pressing Escape cancels it. Saving an empty box removes the link.
sections.why: Likely reason: keyboard shortcuts let an admin edit links quickly.
sections.watch_out: Saving an empty box deletes the stored link without a confirmation step.

sections.name: MilestonesTab (part 1)
sections.title: Milestones table rows
sections.what: Shows a table of project milestones with planned, revised and actual dates. The delay column compares the revised or planned date with the actual date, and shows late results in red.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes slippage against the plan easy to spot.
sections.watch_out: Whether a row is marked late depends on the text from computeDelta starting with a plus sign, so changing that output format would break the highlighting.

sections.name: MilestonesTab (part 2)
sections.title: Milestone status badge and empty state
sections.what: Shows each milestone's status as a badge, with underscores replaced by spaces. Shows a message when no milestones exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: the badge style signals completed, pending or other states at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Badge styles depend on exact status words such as COMPLETED and PENDING, so a renamed status silently falls back to the outline style.

sections.name: DeliveryTab (part 1)
sections.title: Delivery stakeholders and delivery model
sections.what: Shows the vendor, EPC contractor and operator, followed by the delivery model, risk allocation and ecosystem. A list of key parties appears when parties exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: these facts explain who carries the work and the risk.
sections.watch_out: Values are shown with the text '[ N/A ]' when missing, so a gap looks like a deliberate blank rather than an error.

sections.name: DeliveryTab (part 2)
sections.title: Supply chain table
sections.what: Shows a table of supply chain components with their supplier and a status badge. Delivered items get a strong badge, items in progress or in transit get a secondary badge, and anything else gets the outline style.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick view of which parts have arrived and which are still on their way.
sections.watch_out: The status badge checks exact words such as DELIVERED and IN_TRANSIT, so a spelling change silently changes the colour.

sections.name: TechnologyTab
sections.title: Reactor technology details
sections.what: Shows reactor type, thermal and electric capacity, fuel type, design generation and designer. If no technology details exist, a message is shown instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the technical identity of the reactor in one place.
sections.watch_out: Capacity values are shown with fixed units, so a missing number would display as the word undefined followed by the unit.

sections.name: IssuesTab (part 1)
sections.title: Issue register table
sections.what: Shows a table of project issues with lifecycle stage, impact, description and evidence references. A message appears when there are no issues.
sections.why: Likely reason: lists risks and problems so a reader can judge how serious they are.
sections.watch_out: Only CRITICAL and HIGH impacts get the red badge, so a MEDIUM or LOW issue looks the same as any other entry.

sections.name: IssuesTab (part 2)
sections.title: Issue evidence reference buttons
sections.what: Shows each evidence reference as a bracketed button. Clicking one opens the matching evidence item, and a dash-style empty mark appears when there are no references.
sections.why: Likely reason: connects each issue to the source that supports it.
sections.watch_out: A button opens nothing if its reference id does not match an evidence item in the data.

sections.name: ScorecardTab (part 1)
sections.title: Scorecard pillar cards
sections.what: Shows one card per scoring pillar, with its title, trend arrow, score out of five and confidence level, plus a score bar. The card holds the lists of positives and negatives.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a structured score that explains the reasons behind it.
sections.watch_out: The score is shown with toFixed, so a pillar missing its score would cause an error on the page.

sections.name: ScorecardTab (part 2)
sections.title: Scorecard positives, negatives and evidence
sections.what: Lists each positive and negative point with its supporting evidence buttons. Shows a NONE label when a pillar has no negatives. A message appears when no scorecard exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reader see both sides of each score and check the evidence behind each point.
sections.watch_out: Evidence is matched using the exact wording of each point, so editing the text of a point breaks its evidence links.

sections.name: SKUMappingTab
sections.title: SKU mapping table
sections.what: Shows a table of SKUs with their ID, category, description and an alignment percentage. Alignment of 90 or more is green, 80 to 89 is plain, and below 80 is amber.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows how well each suggested product or service fits the project's needs.
sections.watch_out: The intro text says a user selects an issue to see SKUs, but no selection code appears in this section, so that feature is not visible here.

sections.name: SourcesTab (part 1)
sections.title: Sources tab linked list and loading
sections.what: Loads the sources already linked to this project, and loads all sources only when the link form is open. It works out which sources are still available to link and sets up the link action.
sections.why: Likely reason: loading the full list only when needed keeps the page fast.
sections.watch_out: The link action is a plain object, not a standard mutation, and its errors are not caught, so a failed link may fail without a visible message.

sections.name: SourcesTab (part 2)
sections.title: Link source form
sections.what: Shows a dropdown of sources not yet linked, labelled with name, type and tier, plus Link and cancel buttons. Link stays disabled until a source is picked.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents linking an empty choice.
sections.watch_out: Only sources not already linked appear, so a source hidden from this list may still be linked to other projects.

sections.name: SourcesTab (part 3)
sections.title: Linked sources table
sections.what: Shows linked sources with name, type, a clickable URL that opens in a new tab, a colour-coded tier and category. A message appears when no sources are linked.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reader see where each project's information comes from and how much to trust it.
sections.watch_out: The colour rules only separate tier 1, tier 2 and the rest, so tiers 3 to 5 look the same.

sections.name: GATE_STATUS_TONE
sections.title: Maturity status colour map
sections.what: Maps each maturity gate status to a colour style: cleared is green, in progress is amber, not started is neutral, and unknown is muted.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives each status a consistent look across the gate cards.
sections.watch_out: A status not in this list falls back to the unknown style, which can hide a new status type.

sections.name: MaturityTab (part 1)
sections.title: Maturity tab header and research button
sections.what: Loads the maturity gates for the project and shows the rolled-up tier, which defaults to CONCEPT. It notes when the project has not been researched yet. Admins get an Auto-Research button that runs research and refreshes the data.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a single summary of how ready the project is, with the detail below it.
sections.watch_out: If loading fails, the tab shows the default tier and empty gates with no error message, which can look like real data.

sections.name: MaturityTab (part 2)
sections.title: Maturity gate cards and evidence drawer
sections.what: Shows one card per maturity gate with its status, rationale, and a View Evidence button when a quote and source exist. Otherwise it says no evidence. The button opens a citation drawer with the quote.
sections.why: Likely reason: each status must be backed by a quoted source before a reader can trust it.
sections.watch_out: The status text is shortened with replace, which changes only the first underscore, so a status with two underscores would still show one underscore.

sections.name: UsdConversionNotes
sections.title: Budget currency conversion notes
sections.what: Shows notes explaining how each budget was converted to US dollars, with the reported figure in quotes. Nothing appears when no notes exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reader see that converted amounts are estimates based on a stated exchange rate.
sections.watch_out: Only planned, actual and generic budget names get friendly labels, so any other field name appears raw on screen.

summary: Shows the full detail page for one capital project, with tabs for overview, updates, milestones, sources and more, each linked to its evidence.
purpose: Lets a reader see everything recorded about one project and check each fact against its source. It also lets a user start a fresh research run for the project.
why: Likely reason: a project has many kinds of data, so tabs keep each kind apart. The design reasons are not stated in the code.
how: 1. Reads the project id from the web address. 2. Fetches the project data and converts it into a display shape. 3. Checks research status every five seconds while a run is active. 4. Shows a spinner while loading, or a missing-data message. 5. Draws the header, key figures and tab bar. 6. Draws the selected tab's content. 7. Opens a side panel with the citation when a source is clicked.
inputs: The project id in the web address, the signed-in user's role, the project data from the server, and related data for companies, sources, maturity and research runs.
outputs: The rendered project page, requests to start research, and citation side panels.
risks: If no id is in the address, the page quietly loads project p-003. The missing-data message names test project ids. The Refresh project button is not limited to admins in the code shown. Many values are untyped, so wrong data shapes will not be caught by the compiler.
debug: If the missing-data message appears, check that the project id exists on the server and that the fetch succeeded. If the refresh button stays on Researching, check the research status response and its active flag. If a tab is blank, check the tab name in the address and that the tab is drawn in the rendering list. If a value shows N/A, check that the field is in the project data and that its evidence is linked.
